newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end higher on softer crown.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end higher on softer crown.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended higher on Monday, particularly the short end, because of a softer crown.
The crown was stung by worries after telecoms group Ericsson's chief executive Lars Ramqvist said it might move its headquarters abroad.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink's statement that there was no majority within his ruling Social Democratic party in favour of Swedish EMU participation in 1999 hurt the crown further.
"I think the weakening mostly is due to Ericsson's plans," one dealer said.
"There is negative sentiment in the market as the crown is getting closer to 4.5900 against the mark but that is the absolute top (the weakest level it is likely to reach)."
The crown softened to 4.5730 crowns to the mark from 4.5315 late on Friday.
While the crown lifted the short end of the market, the long end did not rise as much because stronger foreign markets partly counterbalanced the crown's negative impact.
The six-month T-bill rate jumped eight basis points to 4.34 percent and the ten-year bond yield rose two basis points to 7.22 percent. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006
